answers.children: Cesky Terriers are moderately good with children. Their small size and affectionate nature allow gentle play with kids while their tenacious yet softer temperament compared to other terriers prevents excessive roughness though patience has limits if handling becomes too boisterous. The silky medium coat stays manageable during interactions and their intelligence helps them read family cues during games. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Cesky Terriers can get along with other pets when raised together. Bred to hunt small game and vermin their prey drive leads to chasing smaller animals while their affectionate side supports peaceful coexistence with larger housemates if introductions are careful and boredom is avoided to limit digging or tension.
answers.exercise: Cesky Terriers need around one hour of exercise daily. Without it their tenacious nature and intelligence combine to create mischief such as digging up gardens or rearranging household items while brisk walks through wooded areas or puzzle toys suit their hunting background and problem-solving strengths.
answers.shedding: Cesky Terriers shed lightly year-round. Their medium silky coat lacks the heavy undercoat of many terriers so loose hair remains minimal yet the texture still traps some debris from outdoor hunts in dense forests or burrows which requires regular attention to prevent minor mats in feathering areas.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic but the Cesky Terrier is often suggested for allergy sufferers. The medium silky coat produces less dander than double-coated breeds and its soft texture from the original Scottish and Sealyham Terrier cross reduces shedding impact though regular grooming remains essential to manage any trapped particles from their vermin-hunting activities.
answers.training: Cesky Terriers are moderately easy to train. Their intelligence and excellent problem-solving skills aid learning yet stubbornness during sessions stems from the tenacious hunting drive developed for independent work in Czech forests making consistent guidance necessary to channel their cleverness without boredom leading to digging.
answers.lifespan: Cesky Terriers live 12-15 years. Their compact build from the purposeful mid-20th century cross supports this range while the health robustness from selective breeding for balanced temperament and silky coat protection against brambles contributes to overall vitality in both hunting and family settings.
answers.size: Cesky Terriers reach 13-22 lb and stand 10-13 in tall. This compact build allows them to navigate tight burrows as originally intended while their substantial yet small frame feels sturdy enough for lively play and cuddling on laps without overwhelming indoor spaces or requiring vast areas to roam.
answers.barking: Cesky Terriers do not bark excessively. They alert to disturbances such as strangers or wildlife due to their hunting heritage in Bohemian terrain but remain quieter than many terriers with their reserved approach to new people and focus on tenacious pursuit rather than constant vocalisation.
answers.apartment: Cesky Terriers can live in an apartment. Their adaptability to various living situations combines with moderate energy and lower barking levels to suit smaller homes provided daily mental stimulation prevents boredom-induced digging and their affectionate nature encourages calm indoor settling after outdoor activity.
answers.first-time: Cesky Terriers are not ideal as a first dog. Their stubbornness during training and tendency to dig if bored demand experienced handling to direct their intelligence and tenacious hunting instincts while first-time owners may struggle to meet the consistent outlets needed for their problem-solving strengths and curiosity.
